Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first ground the work in the workspace contract, then inspect the required wake views and inherited rollout evidence before touching the policy. I’m using the `read-wake-visual-signals-first` skill because this is a 3D moving-window target-policy edit, and the explicitly requested `fish-control-primitives` shelf before deciding whether an architectural transfer is warranted.

The inherited bank shows a mature, repeatable speed-reserve baseline (three captures) plus one projected-miss blend that also captures but is slower and scores worse. I’m treating that lower-scoring semantic success as the informative counterexample available in this sample; there is no failed termination among the four assigned solver results. Next I’m checking both visual rows and the numerical traces before choosing a mechanism.

The four assigned solver examples are exact-byte repeats of the same policy, not four competing designs. All four capture from direct-uniform initialization, with a coherent alternating top-down wake and compact oblique Λ2 structures through terminal approach; capture times span 18.205–18.672T and scores vary because the trajectory is weakly nondeterministic. That makes the current intercept-guarded speed reserve the mechanism to preserve, while the remaining issue is terminal steering/clipping—not propulsion or route acquisition. I’m now consulting the bookshelf at the invariant level, as required, before selecting the one architectural addition.

The inherited yaw-brake rollout is the only unreplicated architectural candidate that both preserves the carrier and captures; its sheet remains visually coherent through 18.38T. By contrast, the half-cycle allocator remains self-propelled but turns below the target and exits at 31.49T, so its failure is allocation geometry rather than wake loss. I’ll use an exact yaw-brake replay as the single candidate—an evidence-driven replication test, not a gain tune or a stacked mechanism. The bookshelf’s terminal-control invariant supports the architecture, so I’m reading its source-family notes before recording the required transfer block.

The candidate-specific diagnosis is now recorded before the code change. It frames the yaw brake as an exact replication of a one-capture mechanism against a stronger 4/4 baseline, with explicit load, saturation, wake, and termination falsifiers. I’m applying only that previously evaluated architectural delta; no gains or additional observations are being introduced.

The candidate now exactly replays the prior yaw-brake architecture, and durable guidance has been corrected in two places: the baseline is now recorded as 4/4 assigned captures, and the projected-miss replacement is recorded as the inherited 1/3 negative result. I also added the evidence boundary for yaw braking: replication is warranted, but one capture with no secondary-metric gain is not improvement. Next I’m invoking the workspace’s required check-runner and will repair any contract or guidance-semantic failure it reports.

The required checker found two environmental/workspace issues, while the solver boundary already passes. The guidance check is blocked by a duplicated identical “copied to guidance” marker in the rendered root README; I’m removing that duplicate so the assigned parent is unambiguous. The shell lacks `julia` on `PATH`, so I’m locating the bundled runtime used by earlier workers and will rerun the same lightweight contract with that binary—still no CFD.

The Julia runtime was genuinely absent on the host. I’ve made the official Julia 1.12.6 image available in the local rootless container store and will run only the prescribed finite-action contract against a read-only mount of `solver/`. This is the same lightweight check, not a simulation.

All three mandated checks now pass after the README marker repair: material reusable guidance, finite two-joint Julia contract/schema, and the solver editable-boundary audit. I’m recording those non-CFD facts in the candidate notes and doing one final integrity pass on the exact candidate hash and required file changes.

Produced exactly one candidate: `dogfish3d_speed_reserve_terminal_yaw_brake_v1`.

- [Candidate policy](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1): exact replay of the prior one-capture yaw-brake mechanism for repeatability testing. SHA-256: `3bc7e932...c9bd`.
- [Candidate notes](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1): visual diagnosis, bookshelf transfer block, evidence metrics, and falsification criteria.
- [Reusable guidance](guidance/control_experience.md:104): records the baseline’s 4/4 captures, rejects projected-miss replacement after its 1/3 record, and defines the yaw-brake replication boundary.

All required non-CFD checks pass: guidance semantics/schema, finite two-joint Julia contract, and solver editable boundary. No CFD was run.
